movement_source: row 'Net interest margin (%)', column 30 Jun 20 -> column 30 Jun 21
headline: CBA's Group net interest margin (cash basis, continuing operations) fell 4 bps to 203 bps in FY21 from 207 bps in FY20. The decline was driven by higher liquid assets (-4 bps), weaker asset pricing (-2 bps) from home loan competition and consumer finance mix shift, and lower deposit margins (-3 bps) from cash rate cuts, partially offset by favourable portfolio mix (+2 bps) from higher deposit funding ratios, improved basis risk (+3 bps) from a narrower bill/OIS spread, and stronger Treasury & Markets contribution (+2 bps). Lower earnings on Group capital (-2 bps) also weighed.

drivers.narrative: Higher liquid asset balances increased $20 billion or 12% year-on-year to $195 billion, driven by strong customer deposit growth and higher trading asset balances. These lower-yielding non-lending interest earning assets decreased margin by 4 bps.

Home lending margins were flat (repricing +9 bps offset by switching to fixed/IO loans -5 bps and competition -4 bps). Business lending margins declined 1 bps from COVID-19 repricing actions. Consumer finance margins fell 1 bps from fewer credit card balances earning interest.

Lower earnings on transaction and savings deposits due to cash rate decreases (down 7 bps) were partly offset by higher replicating portfolio benefits (up 2 bps) and lower wholesale funding costs (up 2 bps), netting -3 bps.

Higher average deposit funding ratio (77% vs 71%) from strong transaction and savings deposit growth, customers switching to at-call deposits, and TFF drawdown (+4 bps), partly offset by unfavourable asset mix from declining consumer finance balances (-2 bps).

Margin increased 3 bps from a decrease in the average bank bill/OIS spread, notwithstanding structural reduction in exposure due to strong cash-rate-linked deposit growth and a mix shift towards fixed rate home loans.
Increased margin by 2 bps driven by higher bonds and commodities financing income in Global Markets.

limitations: The walk chart on page 63 of the results presentation corroborates the profit announcement drivers but uses slightly different labels ('Deposit Pricing & Funding' vs 'Funding costs'). Both sources agree on the -4 bps total movement and all seven driver directions.

The KPI table on page 70 shows a different NIM figure (2.60%/2.63%, -3 bps) which appears to be a divisional or alternative measure; the Group NIM from continuing operations (2.03%/2.07%, -4 bps) on page 22 is the correct measure used here.

Sub-component details within drivers (e.g., home loan repricing +9 bps, switching -5 bps, competition -4 bps) are from narrative text and not independently verified against a separate quantitative source.

evidence_records.quote: Liquid assets: Decreased margin by 4 basis points driven by increased lower yielding non-lending interest earning assets, including liquid assets.

Asset pricing: Decreased margin by 2 basis points driven by lower business lending margins (down 1 basis point) from repricing actions to support businesses during COVID-19, and lower consumer finance margins (down 1 basis point) from a reduction in the proportion of interest earning credit card balances. Home lending margins were flat, reflecting repricing (up 9 basis points), offset by the impact of customers switching from higher margin loans to lower margin loans, particularly from variable rate to fixed rate loans (down 5 basis points) and increased competition (down 4 basis points).

Funding costs: Decreased margin by 3 basis points, reflecting lower earnings on transaction and savings deposits mainly due to decreases in the cash rate (down 7 basis points), partly offset by higher benefits from the replicating portfolio (up 2 basis points) and lower wholesale funding costs (up 2 basis points).

Portfolio mix: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by a higher average deposit funding ratio (30 June 2021: 77%; 30 June 2020: 71%) due to strong growth in transaction and savings deposits, customers switching to at-call deposits, and the drawdown of the TFF (up 4 basis points), partly offset by an unfavourable impact from asset mix (down 2 basis points), mainly due to a decline in higher margin consumer finance balances.

Basis risk: Basis risk arises from the spread between the 3 month bank bill swap rate and the 3 month overnight index swap rate. The Bank's margin increased 3 basis points reflecting a decrease in the average spread notwithstanding a structural reduction in exposure to basis risk due to strong growth in cash rate linked deposits and a mix shift towards fixed rate home loans.

Capital and other: Decreased margin by 2 basis points driven by lower earnings on Group capital due to the falling interest rate environment (down 3 basis points), partly offset by increased contribution from New Zealand (up 1 basis point), reflecting lower wholesale funding costs and favourable portfolio mix, partly offset by the impact from RBNZ cash rate cuts.
Treasury and Markets: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by higher bonds and commodities financing income in Global Markets.
Group margin1 Flat ex liquids – pressure from lower interest rates, offset by favourable portfolio mix, lower wholesale funding costs

Net interest margin (NIM) decreased 4 basis points due to higher liquid assets, with the impact of the low-rate environment on deposit margins and earnings on capital largely offset by the benefit from lower wholesale funding costs and favourable funding mix
